test_title: RRB Group D Official Paper (Held On: 30 Dec, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Select the statement regarding cell organelles that is INCORRECT.

options.text: Each cell organelle performs a special function.
They are found in Eukaryotic cells.
They are found in Prokaryotic cells.

solution:
The correct answer is __**They are found in Prokaryotic cells**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Cell organelles** are specialized, internal organized structures within a living cell that perform specific **metabolic functions**. Examples include the **nucleus**, **mitochondria**, **ribosomes**, and **endoplasmic reticulum**.
 
• **Statement 1**: "Each cell organelle performs a special function." Organelles act like the "organs" of the cell; for instance, **mitochondria** are responsible for **cellular respiration** and **ATP** production, while **chloroplasts** in plants handle **photosynthesis**. ***Hence, statement 1 is correct.***
 
• **Statement 2**: "They are found in Eukaryotic cells." The defining characteristic of **eukaryotic cells** (found in **plants**, **animals**, **fungi**, and **protists**) is the presence of a **well-defined nucleus** and membrane-bound organelles. ***Hence, statement 2 is correct.***
 
• **Statement 3**: "They are membrane-bound structures." Most organelles in complex cells are enclosed by **lipid membranes** to separate different chemical reactions from each other, ensuring **cellular efficiency**. ***Hence, statement 3 is correct.***
 
• **Statement 4**: "They are found in Prokaryotic cells." **Prokaryotic cells**, such as **bacteria** and **archaea**, lack a **true nucleus** and membrane-bound organelles. While they contain **ribosomes**, these are not membrane-bound. They do not possess **mitochondria**, **lysosomes**, or **Golgi bodies**. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***
 
• ***Therefore, the incorrect statement regarding cell organelles is that they are found in prokaryotic cells.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Prokaryotic Cells:**
 
 
• These cells are generally small, typically ranging from **0.1 to 5.0 micrometers** in diameter.
 
• Their **DNA** is found in a region called the **nucleoid** and is usually **circular**.
 
• They contain **70S ribosomes** but lack internal compartmentalization.
 
 
 
• **Eukaryotic Cells:**
 
 
• These are larger and more complex, usually **10 to 100 micrometers** in size.
 
• They possess **linear DNA** organized into **chromosomes** within a **nuclear envelope**.
 
• They contain **80S ribosomes** in the **cytoplasm** and **70S ribosomes** within certain organelles like **mitochondria**.
 
 
 
• **Major Organelles and Functions:**
 
 
• **Nucleus:** Known as the **"Control Center"** of the cell, it contains **genetic material**.
 
• **Mitochondria:** Known as the **"Powerhouse of the Cell"** where **ATP** (Adenosine Triphosphate) is generated.
 
• **Lysosomes:** Often called **"Suicide Bags"** because they contain **digestive enzymes** to break down waste.
 
• **Endoplasmic Reticulum (ER):** The **Rough ER** is involved in **protein synthesis**, while the **Smooth ER** is involved in **lipid synthesis**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Cell Theory:** Proposed by **Matthias Schleiden** and **Theodor Schwann** in **1838-1839**, stating that all living things are composed of cells. **Rudolf Virchow** later added in **1855** that all cells arise from **pre-existing cells**.
 
• **Discovery:** The cell was first discovered and named by **Robert Hooke** in **1665** using a primitive microscope to observe **cork**.
 
• **Ribosomes:** These are unique because they are found in **both prokaryotes and eukaryotes**. They are the site of **protein synthesis** and are not surrounded by a membrane, which is why they are often referred to as **non-membranous organelles**.
 
• **Endosymbiotic Theory:** This theory suggests that **mitochondria** and **chloroplasts** were once free-living **prokaryotic organisms** that were engulfed by a larger cell, leading to the evolution of **eukaryotic cells**.
</ul
